pr.title: Type-check the hooks module in the local gate
pr.head: 2a5af53163bf85daa8008233dacf8dffad3f41c8

summary: Projector ships a Claude Code hooks module in hooks/: TypeScript that draws Projector's band above the prompt and reads the inbox. Claude Code compiles and runs it, but the validation gate never type-checked it. claude plugin validate . and claude plugin test . both pass code that tsc rejects, which is how the type error that #287 fixed reached main.
This change adds hooks/typecheck.sh to the local gate. The script runs the TypeScript compiler that site/ already installs, through a new root tsconfig.json that covers only hooks/.

The compiler needs Claude Code's own declarations: the claude-code module, its claude-code/testing kit, and the inputs of the built-in tools. Claude Code writes them to .claude-plugin/types/ when an interactive session loads a checkout with claude --plugin-dir ., and nothing else provides them. So the check runs only in the local gate, and the Check workflow in CI does not run it. A linked worktree with no declarations of its own borrows the main checkout's. When neither checkout has them, the step fails with a setup message.

cards.title: Set up a checkout once
cards.html:
1. Run npm ci in site/, which installs tsc.
  2. Start claude --plugin-dir . from the repository root and quit at the prompt. Claude Code writes the declarations to .claude-plugin/types/, which Git ignores. A linked worktree can skip this step when the main checkout has them.
  3. Run hooks/typecheck.sh. Repeat step 2 after you update Claude Code.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• Two Projector reviews, of c38d3b1 and of 2a5af53, found each head clean, with no finding threads.
  • 2a5af53 added the borrow from the main checkout. Its review tested the borrow in a throwaway clone with a linked worktree.
  • Neither review could get declarations that Claude Code wrote. Both ran the check against a copy rebuilt from the declarations Claude Code 2.1.296 bundles with its plugin-authoring skill.

groups.title: The type check and its configuration
groups.kicker: A gate script, the root tsconfig it compiles with, and the ignore rule for the declarations
intro: hooks/typecheck.sh first checks that site/ has tsc. When this checkout has the declarations, the script runs tsc -p . from the repository root. When it has none, the script takes the main checkout, the first entry git worktree list prints, and borrows the declarations from there. To borrow them, it writes a tsconfig.json to a temporary directory that extends the main checkout's declarations and includes this worktree's hooks/. It deletes that directory on exit. The script exits 1 with a setup instruction when the compiler or the declarations are missing, and otherwise exits with the compiler's status, 2 on a type error.

The root tsconfig.json extends the tsconfig.json Claude Code writes in .claude-plugin/types/. That file carries the compiler options a hooks module needs, such as JSX compiled to h, and makes the folder the type root. The root file only narrows include to hooks. It sits at the root because Claude Code writes its own root tsconfig.json into a plugin that has none, and a committed one stops that untracked file from appearing.

checks.text: The check catches the errors it exists for. With declarations rebuilt from Claude Code 2.1.296's bundled copy, the head exits 0. A deliberate error in hooks/parse.ts exits 2 with TS2322, and the hooks/ tree from 7e0a5e0 exits 2 with the one hooks/register.tsx(282,60) error that #287 fixed.

The root tsconfig.json does not change how Claude Code loads the plugin. With .claude-plugin/types/ removed, as in an installed copy, claude plugin test . passes all 78 tests. A root tsconfig.json with a bogus jsxFactory also passes them, so the engine does not read the file at load time.

files.note: The gate step: checks for tsc, then type-checks hooks/ against this checkout's declarations or, failing that, the main checkout's.

checks.text: The script tests only that a tsconfig.json exists in .claude-plugin/types/. Declarations written by an older Claude Code pass this test, which is why the documentation says to start a session again after an update.

This comment says the declarations depend only on the Claude Code version. The engine's reference says the folder also holds the MCP tools connected when the session loaded and the contracts of the plugins in dependencies. A borrowed copy reflects the main checkout's versions of those, though no code in hooks/ reads either one today. The review listed this as a suggestion.
With no declarations in either checkout, the script exits 1 with this message. The review's scratch worktree reproduced it.

The borrow works and checks the right code. In a throwaway clone with a linked worktree, the script names the main checkout and exits 0. An error added to the worktree's hooks/parse.ts exits 2, so the status survives the EXIT trap. The same error added only to the main checkout passes. The temporary directory is gone after both runs, and a worktree path with a space and a double quote still works.

files.note: Extends Claude Code's generated tsconfig.json and limits the program to hooks/.

checks.text: site/ keeps its own tsconfig.json, so npm run check in site/ still passes with this file at the root.

files.note: Ignores .claude-plugin/types/, which Claude Code writes into the checkout.

groups.title: Gate documentation
groups.kicker: Where contributors learn about the new step and its one-time setup
intro: Three documents list the gate, and each now lists hooks/typecheck.sh and says that a linked worktree borrows the main checkout's declarations. AGENTS.md is the file agents follow, and CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it. docs/develop.md turns the old one-line npm ci reminder into two setup steps. docs/plugins.md adds the step to the checks a plugin author runs before publishing.

files.note: Adds the step to the gate and explains why CI cannot run it.
Two setup steps before the gate, and a note that the Check workflow cannot type-check hooks/.

checks.text: The claim that Projector loads only with gh-stack installed matches dependencies in .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the plugins.md#install-for-claude-code anchor resolves.

files.note: Adds the step to the plugin checks, linking to the setup in docs/develop.md.
